data: Mosaic floor recording works dedicated to Venus
orthography suggests late Republican date, perhaps late 2nd century BCE
Found in Syracuse, 11 February 1576 in the square of the no-longer extant S.Margarita, Piazza de Montedoro, an earlier name for Piazza d'Armi, in the vicinity of the ancient Roman forum

Apparatus criticus

  • Text of Gaggiotti 2002

English translation

Jonathan Prag

Cnaeus Octavius, son of Aulus, officer and administrator of the company of fishmongers made the pavement and benches and saw to the restoration of the temple of Venus Tarichina (Venus of the Saltworks)

commentary

The mosaic is lost, and modern readings are dependent upon an unsatisfactory text recorded in the antiquarian tradition
